# Physical fiber inclusions from the volume martingale, and a support-slack limitation

This is an exact geometric consequence of the audited ell-tight base-volume martingale. It preserves the ORIGINAL full-volume target, gives actual Minkowski inclusions after a projective rescaling, and identifies a boundary-normal slack through mixed volumes. A rational three-fiber example shows that zero integrated source-area support slack can coexist with a strict transported-volume deficit, even with all strict closed-minor quotas, an actual proper deepest source, and a uniquely optimal concave parameter. The example is safely above the OC threshold and is not a joint body minimum or a physical-response dual certificate.

## 1. Exact original-volume transport after rescaling

Let positive compatible fibers K_z have masses V_z, total M, and w_z=V_z/M. Let ell_z>0 be sampled-concave, and suppose the parameter theorem supplies sigma supported on J, sum sigma=1, and an ell-tight base martingale pi with

    mu_p=sigma_p/ell_p,     nu_z=w_z/ell_z,
    sum_z pi_pz=mu_p,      sum_p pi_pz=nu_z,
    sum_z pi_pz z=mu_p p,
    sum_z pi_pz ell_z=mu_p ell_p.                       (1)

For a positive source row define

    hatpi_pz=ell_z pi_pz,
    alpha_pz=hatpi_pz/sigma_p,
    Z_z=(z,1)/ell_z,
    D_z=K_z/ell_z.                                     (2)

Then hatpi is a probability coupling from sigma to the ORIGINAL volume weights w, and

    sum_z alpha_pz Z_z=Z_p,
    sum_z alpha_pz D_z subset D_p.                     (3)

The first assertion follows from the ell moment in (1) and the column marginal. Its projective coordinate identity follows by canceling ell_z in both the z and final 1 coordinates. For the body inclusion, put lambda_pz=pi_pz/mu_p. Compatibility gives sum_z lambda_pz K_z subset K_p. Dividing by ell_p and using alpha_pz=lambda_pz ell_z/ell_p proves (3). This is an actual Minkowski inclusion, not a transport of uniform fiber laws.

The last coordinate in Z is retained. In general z/ell_z alone does not preserve all base information. On an ell supporting contact plane, these are the usual affine coordinates on its projective image; no global injectivity is needed for (3).

Consequently, for every continuous normal u the support array h_(D_z)(u) is a supermartingale along this SAME hatpi, and Brunn–Minkowski gives

    R_p>=sum_z alpha_pz R_z,
    R_z=V_z^(1/d)/ell_z.                               (4)

In particular

    sum_p sigma_p R_p>=sum_z w_z R_z.                  (5)

The right marginal here is the original full family. Equality or a bound for (5) is not supplied by the parameter theorem. Marked-fiber homothety on genuine source-source anchored relations remains compatible with (3), but does not turn the source-to-all-target inclusions into equalities.

## 2. An exact normal-area and mixed-volume identity

For each positive source let

    B_p=sum_z alpha_pz D_z subset D_p,
    s_p(u)=h_(D_p)(u)-sum_z alpha_pz h_(D_z)(u)>=0.

Write S_D for the surface-area measure of a positive d-body D. In d>=2, the standard first mixed-volume formula, or its defining support integral, gives

    integral s_p(u) dS_(D_p)(u)
       =d[ |D_p|-sum_z alpha_pz V(D_z,D_p[d-1]) ]>=0.   (6)

Multiplication by sigma_p and summation is legitimate and retains one source surface measure per row. In particular the second term is

    d sum_(p,z) hatpi_pz V(D_z,D_p[d-1]),

NOT d sum_z w_z |D_z|. Replacing a mixed volume by a target volume would change the actual normal marginal and is not justified by (1).

For d=1 the same identity holds with mixed volume V(D_z,D_p[0])=|D_z| and H_0 surface measure at the two endpoint normals. The counterexample below uses d=2, where tangential face geometry is present.

If a positive measure has full support on the unit sphere, zero integral of the continuous nonnegative s_p forces s_p identically zero and B_p=D_p. Source surface-area measures need not have full spherical support. In particular for polytopes, (6)=0 asserts equality only at their facet normals. Even B_p=D_p alone would not imply equality in the separate Brunn–Minkowski bound (4). These are different equality requirements.

## 3. A rational canonical three-fiber family

Take n=1,d=2, P={-1,0,1}, and

    K=[-1,1]^2,
    D=K intersect {|x_1|+|x_2|<=3/2},
    K_0=K,       K_(-1)=K_1=D.                         (7)

Then |K|=4, |D|=7/2, M=11, k(P)=2. The fibers are compatible because D subset K. Their canonical convex hull has exactly these integer fibers; on each adjacent base interval it has the actual Minkowski interpolation of D and K.

Every strict proper closed-minor quota holds. The three singleton masses are 7/2,4,7/2, all below M/2=11/2. The only other nonempty proper closed minors are the adjacent pairs, each of mass 15/2<M because it has both parities. The endpoint pair is not closed.

Let ell=1 and sigma=delta_0. The unique one-source martingale with the required target is

    pi_(0,-1)=7/22,    pi_(0,0)=4/11,    pi_(0,1)=7/22. (8)

It preserves both base and ell. Its normalized bodies D_z in (2) are simply the original bodies. The actual transported source body is

    B_0=(4/11)K+(7/11)D
       =K intersect {|x_1|+|x_2|<=37/22}.              (9)

To verify the equality, both summands have the same eight possible outward edge normals, with axis support one and diagonal support respectively 2 and 3/2 in unnormalized diagonal coordinates. Their Minkowski sum has exactly the corresponding combined supports. Equivalently the support functions agree on the common fan and hence everywhere.

The four corner triangles removed from K in (9) have leg length 7/22. Therefore

    |K|-|B_0|=4*(1/2)*(7/22)^2=49/242>0.              (10)

But S_K places mass 2 at each of the four unit axis normals, and at all four

    h_K=h_D=h_(B_0)=1.

Thus s_0 vanishes S_K-almost everywhere and (6) is EXACTLY ZERO. The same is true after multiplication by any bounded boundary density: the scalar support slack is already zero at every regular boundary normal of K. This does not assert a tangential boundary coupling. For example each vertical face of B_0 has length 15/11, strictly less than the corresponding length 2 in K; the lost end pieces of the facet are genuine geometry invisible to the scalar support equality.

## 4. Actual deepestness and a genuine parameter optimum

At epsilon=0 the full mixed set in (7) is centrally symmetric about (0,0), and every nonvertical hyperplane through this point has zero mixed boundary mass. Its two closed halfspaces have equal mass M/2=11/2. Pure-base caps through base zero have mass |K|+|D|=15/2. Thus the actual mixed depth at (0,0) is exactly 11/2.

It is the unique deepest mark. At an endpoint base a pure-base isolating cap has mass 7/2<11/2. At a nonzero middle mark y, take u=y and base tilt zero: the cap {u.X>=u.y} loses a positive-volume strip of K compared with its through-zero counterpart of mass M/2. Hence its mass is strictly below M/2. This proof retains every competing source and provides actual all-normal lower and upper certificates.

Now fix 0<epsilon<=1/10 and use the covariance buffer and ell=1. Each fiber is centrally symmetric in X, so buffered depth on the middle fiber is even. Its superlevels are convex; hence zero is a maximizing mark there. Endpoint base depths remain at most 7/2 for every buffer. The middle value is at least 11/2, so the global maximizing base is still zero.

For an explicit proper-gap upper bound, symmetry gives covariance Sigma=(79/264)I. Indeed integral_K x_1^2=4/3, while integral_D x_1^2=47/48, giving (4/3+2*(47/48))/11=79/264. At the middle centroid E_K(0)=4, so its unit-axis threshold radius is

    delta=epsilon (4/11)^(1/3) sqrt(79/264)<epsilon.

For delta<1/2, all three central vertical section lengths equal 2. The zero-base-tilt axis cap therefore has exact mass

    11/2+6 delta<11/2+3/5<15/2=b_base(0).             (11)

Thus the actual source is proper-gap; strict fixed-fiber concavity and an active proper cap give its uniqueness, as in the nonregular heredity theorem.

Finally ell=1 is the UNIQUE global minimizer over all positive sampled-concave arrays with weighted geometric mean one, with this BODY fixed. Write their values as a,b,c at -1,0,1. Concavity gives b>=(a+c)/2 and normalization gives

    0=(7/22)(log a+log c)+(4/11)log b
       <=(7/11)log[(a+c)/2]+(4/11)log b<=log b.

Hence b>=1, with equality only a=b=c=1. The middle maximum depends only on b. It increases strictly above its value at b=1 when b>1: equality would contradict the strict scalar monotonicity lemma, since the common value would remain below the atomic bound by (11). The endpoints never exceed 7/2, so they cannot change this conclusion. Thus (8) occurs at an actual concave-PARAMETER optimum with an actual proper deepest source, not merely at arbitrary numerical weights.

Its normalized depth is at least 1/2, safely above Gamma_2/k(P)=2/9. No JOINT body minimum, bad-depth premise, surface-response dual, or uniform conditional fiber lift has been established or claimed.

## 5. Consequence for the proposed geometric bridge

The projective rescaling (2) genuinely retains original-volume marginals and actual Minkowski inclusions. Formula (6) is the corresponding exact boundary-normal identity. However even the strongest possible conclusion of zero scalar support slack in this source area measure would leave the positive deficit (10). Any bridge to whole-fiber equality or a numerical payment must also control tangential face geometry, a full-support normal measure, or a separate volume/Brunn–Minkowski equality defect. The volume martingale itself supplies none of these additional equalities.
